identity.title: Exchangeability of GNN Representations with Applications to Graph Retrieval

problem.claim: The paper addresses efficient approximation of transportation-based graph similarities and locality-sensitive hashing for graph retrieval.

contributions.claim: Characterizes exchangeability in trained node embeddings produced by a large family of GNNs under standard optimization tools.

Uses order-statistic Euclidean similarities to approximate transportation-based graph similarities and proposes a unified LSH framework covering measures such as subgraph matching and graph edit distance.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that they discover a probabilistic symmetry, exchangeability, in GNNs and derive a unified LSH framework from it.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their method performs LSH more effectively than baselines in experiments.

narrative_sequence.summary: Introduces exchangeability as a probabilistic symmetry in GNNs.
States that trained node embeddings are exchangeable, yielding permutation-invariant embedding densities and identical distributions across representation elements.
Reduces transportation-based similarity approximation to Euclidean comparisons of order statistics and builds a multi-measure LSH framework.
Reports more effective LSH than baselines in experiments.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a representation-level symmetry to a retrieval method by first stating the invariance, then describing the resulting similarity reduction and its LSH application.

lessons.interpretation: A structural property becomes a persuasive method motivation when its operational consequence is stated explicitly.
lessons.application: When proposing a retrieval algorithm, connect each representation property to a concrete distance or indexing reduction before presenting the system.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the proposed representation property has no demonstrated computational consequence or the reduction requires unstated assumptions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the GNN architectures, optimization assumptions, approximation guarantees, datasets, metrics, baseline identities, or the magnitude of experimental improvements.
The conditions under which the claimed exchangeability and similarity approximation hold are not detailed.
